items.a: BiblioFuse Reader handles comics, manga, PDFs, EPUB and TXT in one library — including large mixed collections you stream from your own Mac or PC. Everything is processed on your device: no upload, no account, and no tracking of what you read.

items.q: Do my files upload to BiblioFuse servers?
items.a: No. The apps are built around on-device work. Reading, compression, duplicate scanning, and browser tools process files locally. Sync and streaming use your own iCloud, local network, or Tailscale setup rather than a BiblioFuse account.
Most BiblioFuse apps are free to try or have free limits, with optional paid upgrades for heavier use. Store pages show the current pricing for each platform.

items.q: Does one purchase cover all platforms?
items.a: No. iOS + Mac is a single universal purchase — one payment covers iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Vision Pro. The Android Reader, PC Reader, and PC tools are each sold separately.

seo.desc: SmartDecrypt auto-unlocks PDF, ZIP, and 7z files using saved filename patterns — perfect for bank statements, insurance docs, and invoices that always use the same password format. Drop the file, it finds the right password automatically.

faq.q: What file formats does SmartDecrypt support?
faq.a: PDF, ZIP, and 7z. Unencrypted ZIP and 7z archives are extracted normally without asking for a password. SmartDecrypt does not currently support RAR, EPUB, or other formats.

faq.q: Does SmartDecrypt bypass unknown passwords?
faq.a: No. SmartDecrypt is designed for files you already have permission to access. It uses passwords you have saved in a profile — it does not crack or brute-force unknown passwords.

faq.q: Are my passwords safe?
faq.a: Yes. Passwords are stored exclusively in the system Keychain on your device — the same secure storage used by Safari and your other apps. SmartDecrypt never stores passwords in its own database, and nothing is uploaded to any server.

faq.q: What is a filename pattern?
faq.a: A filename pattern is a partial name or keyword that identifies recurring files. For example, if your bank sends monthly statements named 'BankStatement_2024-01.pdf', create a profile with the pattern 'BankStatement' and the password. SmartDecrypt matches future files to that profile automatically.

faq.q: Is the Pro purchase shared between iPhone and Mac?
faq.a: Yes. SmartDecrypt Pro is a one-time universal purchase. Buy once on either iOS or macOS and unlock Pro on both platforms using the same Apple ID.

faq.q: Is ContentCue an ad blocker?
faq.a: No. ContentCue does not block, hide, or prevent ads from loading. All advertisements display normally. ContentCue improves navigation by saving your scroll position when ads interrupt your reading, and it draws colored borders around in-page ads so you can see them clearly.

faq.q: Which sites does ContentCue work with?
faq.a: ContentCue is a full web browser, so it works with any website — Webtoons, Tapas, LINE Webtoon, independent creator pages, manga aggregators, WordPress blogs, and thousands more. No per-site setup is needed.

faq.q: How does position restore work?
faq.a: ContentCue monitors your scroll position while you read. When you navigate away (tapping an ad link, a redirect, or the back button), it saves your exact position. A Resume button appears in the browser UI. Tap it to return to exactly where you were.

faq.q: Does ContentCue have an RSS reader?
faq.a: Yes. Subscribe to any RSS feed, pin your favourite channels, and import or export your whole subscription list via OPML. Turn on TTS to hear your unread headlines read aloud as one continuous audio briefing, like a personal radio update.

faq.q: Can I listen to podcasts in ContentCue?
faq.a: Yes. Search the built-in podcast directory, pin the shows you follow, and stream or download episodes to listen offline. Playback works from the lock screen and includes a built-in sleep timer.

faq.q: Does ContentCue read web pages aloud?
faq.a: Yes. Tap Play on any article and ContentCue reads it aloud with text-to-speech. Background audio keeps playing when your screen is locked, and the app quickly resumes your last article and position.

faq.q: Does ContentCue sync across my iPhone, iPad, and Vision Pro?
faq.a: Yes, with Premium. Bookmarks, RSS feeds, and podcast subscriptions sync automatically via iCloud across all your Apple devices, including Apple Vision Pro.

faq.q: Does ContentCue work on Apple Vision Pro?
faq.a: Yes. ContentCue has a native visionOS app — browse in a floating window, page through articles with a quick pinch, and shrink playback to a compact corner player. It’s a universal purchase: buy once and use it on iPhone, iPad, and Vision Pro, with Premium shared across all three.

faq.q: Does ContentCue support CarPlay?
faq.a: Yes. ContentCue appears on your car’s CarPlay display with your saved podcasts and RSS feeds. You can start playback, see the current queue, and change playback speed directly from the car screen.

faq.q: Does ContentCue collect my browsing data?
faq.a: No. ContentCue processes all browsing entirely on your device using Apple WebKit. No browsing history, visited URLs, or personal data is collected or transmitted anywhere.

faq.q: What does ContentCue Premium include?
faq.a: Free includes the full reading browser plus up to 3 bookmarks, 3 RSS feeds, and 3 saved podcast shows. Premium removes those limits — unlimited bookmarks, feeds, and shows — and adds iCloud Sync across devices, Siri Shortcuts, custom ad outline colours, and adjustable auto-scroll speed. It’s available as a yearly subscription with a 7-day free trial, or a one-time lifetime purchase.

toolsHub.seoTitle: Free Browser Tools for Comics & Ebooks — CBZ, EPUB, PDF
toolsHub.seoDesc: Free tools for comic and ebook files that run entirely in your browser: shrink CBZ archives, compress EPUBs, convert PDF to CBZ or JPG. No upload, no account.
toolsHub.intro: Small tools for the file formats BiblioFuse reads. Each one runs entirely inside your browser — the file never leaves your device, and there is nothing to install or sign up for.

toolsPages.appPitch: BiblioFuse reads CBZ, CBR, EPUB, PDF and TXT on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Android and Windows — and streams big libraries straight from your own machine.

cbz-reducer.cardDesc: Shrink comic archives by re-encoding the pages inside, without splitting the volume.
cbz-reducer.seoTitle: Reduce CBZ File Size — Free, In Your Browser, No Upload
cbz-reducer.seoDesc: Compress CBZ and ZIP comic archives in your browser. Re-encodes the pages inside at a resolution and quality you choose. Nothing is uploaded — the whole job runs on your device.
cbz-reducer.intro: Drop in a CBZ or ZIP and it re-encodes every page inside at the size and quality you pick, then hands the archive back. Large scans usually lose most of their weight with no visible difference on a phone screen.

sections.title: Why comic archives get so big
sections.body: A CBZ is just a ZIP full of page images. Scans are often stored at print resolution — 3000px wide or more — which is far beyond what any phone or tablet can display. Re-encoding those pages to the resolution you actually read at is usually where the savings come from, not the archive format.

sections.title: What the settings do
sections.body: Shortest-dimension resolution caps the smaller side of each page, so tall pages and spreads scale consistently. Quality controls the encoder. Grayscale drops colour channels entirely, which helps a lot on black-and-white manga and nothing at all on colour comics.

sections.title: Nothing leaves your device
sections.body: The archive is opened, re-encoded and rebuilt inside your browser using WebAssembly. There is no upload step, no queue and no server that ever sees the file — which also means it works on files you would not want to hand to a web service.

faq.q: Will this ruin the image quality?
faq.a: Only if you tell it to. The default settings target the resolution a phone or tablet actually renders at, which is well below what most scans are stored at, so the visible result is usually identical. If you archive at print quality, raise the resolution cap or leave the file alone.

faq.q: Does it work on CBR or RAR files?
faq.a: No — CBR is a RAR archive, and RAR cannot be opened in the browser for licensing reasons. Convert to CBZ first, or use the BiblioFuse app, which reads CBR directly.

faq.q: Is there a file size limit?
faq.a: The limit is your device's memory, not a server quota, because the work happens locally. Very large volumes are fine on a desktop; a phone with several hundred megabytes of pages may run out of room.

epub-reducer.cardDesc: Re-encode the images inside an EPUB so it syncs and stores smaller.
epub-reducer.seoTitle: Compress EPUB Files — Free, In Your Browser, No Upload
epub-reducer.seoDesc: Shrink EPUB files by re-encoding the images inside them, in your browser. Text and structure are left untouched. No upload, no account, nothing sent to a server.
epub-reducer.intro: Drop in an EPUB and it re-encodes the images inside — covers, illustrations, embedded scans — while leaving the text, structure and metadata exactly as they were.

sections.title: It is almost always the images
sections.body: The text in a novel-length EPUB is tiny — often under a megabyte. When an EPUB is large, it is because of embedded images stored at far higher resolution than any reader will display. Re-encoding those is where the size goes.

sections.title: What is left alone
sections.body: Chapter structure, table of contents, metadata and the text itself are untouched — they are copied through unchanged. Only the image files inside the archive are re-encoded, so the book opens and navigates exactly as before.

sections.title: Nothing leaves your device
sections.body: The EPUB is unpacked, processed and repacked inside your browser. No copy is uploaded, which matters for books you own but would rather not hand to a web service.

faq.q: Will it break DRM-protected books?
faq.a: It cannot open them at all. DRM-protected EPUBs are encrypted, so there is nothing to re-encode. This works on DRM-free files only.

faq.q: Does the text get compressed too?
faq.a: No. Text is copied through untouched — it is a negligible share of the file size and re-encoding it would risk breaking the book's structure for no gain.

faq.q: Will my reader still open it?
faq.a: Yes. The output is a standard EPUB with the same structure and metadata as the input; only the image files inside are smaller.

pdf-to-cbz.cardDesc: Turn a PDF comic into a CBZ so comic readers can page through it properly.
pdf-to-cbz.seoTitle: Convert PDF to CBZ — Free, In Your Browser, No Upload
pdf-to-cbz.seoDesc: Convert PDF comics and scans to CBZ in your browser. Each page is rendered to an image and packed into a comic archive. No upload, no account, nothing sent to a server.
pdf-to-cbz.intro: Drop in a PDF and every page is rendered to an image and packed into a CBZ, so comic readers can treat it as a proper page-by-page volume instead of a document.

sections.title: Why convert at all
sections.body: PDF is a document format. Comic readers built around CBZ get page-spread detection, reading direction, thumbnail grids and per-page bookmarks — features a PDF viewer generally does not offer for scanned comics.

sections.title: What you get out
sections.body: A standard CBZ: a ZIP of sequentially numbered page images. Pages are rendered at 2× scale so text and line art stay sharp when you zoom, then encoded to a web-friendly format.

sections.title: Nothing leaves your device
sections.body: Rendering and packing both happen in your browser. The PDF is never uploaded, so this is safe to use on scans and documents you would not want to put through a web service.

faq.q: Does the text stay searchable?
faq.a: No. CBZ is an image format by definition, so any selectable text in the PDF becomes part of the page image. If you need text search, keep the PDF — or read it in BiblioFuse, which can OCR pages on device.

faq.q: What resolution are the pages rendered at?
faq.a: 2× the PDF's native page size, which keeps line art and lettering sharp when zoomed. Larger PDFs therefore take longer and use more memory.

faq.q: Can it convert back the other way?
faq.a: Not here — this direction covers the common case of a PDF that ought to be a comic. The BiblioFuse app handles CBZ to PDF on device.

pdf-to-jpg.cardDesc: Export every page of a PDF as an image, downloaded as a ZIP.
pdf-to-jpg.seoTitle: Convert PDF to JPG — Free, In Your Browser, No Upload
pdf-to-jpg.seoDesc: Export PDF pages as JPG images in your browser and download them as a ZIP. Pick the render quality. No upload, no account, nothing sent to a server.
pdf-to-jpg.intro: Drop in a PDF and every page is rendered to a JPG at the quality you choose, then bundled into a single ZIP download.

sections.title: What it is for
sections.body: Pulling pages out as images — for a slide, a reference sheet, an issue report, or any workflow that wants pictures rather than a document. Every page is exported; there is no per-page selection step.

sections.title: Choosing quality
sections.body: The quality control is the render scale, not just the encoder setting. Higher values render each page larger before encoding, which keeps small text legible at the cost of file size and processing time.

sections.title: Nothing leaves your device
sections.body: Rendering uses the PDF engine built into the page and runs entirely in your browser. The file is never uploaded — which is the point if the PDF is a statement, a contract, or anything else you would not paste into a web tool.

faq.q: Can I export just one page?
faq.a: Not currently — every page is exported and delivered as a ZIP. Extract the one you need from the archive.

faq.q: Why JPG and not PNG?
faq.a: JPG is dramatically smaller for scanned and photographic pages, which is the common case. For line art or screenshots where you want lossless output, PDF to CBZ preserves more detail.

faq.q: Does it work on password-protected PDFs?
faq.a: No. An encrypted PDF has to be unlocked before anything can render it. SmartDecrypt, a separate app from the same studio, handles that case.

qr-generator.cardDesc: Make a setup QR code so the app can connect to your server without typing.
qr-generator.seoTitle: Kavita & Komga Setup QR Code Generator
qr-generator.seoDesc: Generate a QR code that points BiblioFuse at your Kavita or Komga server, so you do not have to type a URL and API key on a phone. Built in your browser; nothing is sent anywhere.
qr-generator.intro: Fill in your server details and get a QR code the app can scan — no typing a long URL and API key on a phone keyboard.

sections.title: Why a QR code
sections.body: A self-hosted server address plus an API key is a long, error-prone thing to type on a phone. Scanning a code gets both across in one step, correctly, every time.

sections.title: Your key never leaves the page
sections.body: The code is drawn in your browser from the values you type. Nothing is submitted, logged or stored — close the tab and it is gone. The generated image is only as private as wherever you choose to put it, so treat a printed code like the API key it contains.

faq.q: Is my API key sent anywhere?
faq.a: No. The QR code is generated locally in the page and the values you type are never transmitted or saved. Do bear in mind the finished code contains your key, so anyone who can photograph it can use it.

faq.q: Which servers does this support?
faq.a: Kavita and Komga. Pick the service type and the default port fills in; adjust the address if your setup differs.

guidePage.seoTitle: BiblioFuse Guide - Setup, Streaming, Libraries & Troubleshooting
guidePage.seoDesc: How to set up BiblioFuse: adding books, connecting Kavita, Komga and OPDS libraries, streaming from your own Mac or PC, reading options, and fixing common problems.
guidePage.intro: Setup, streaming and troubleshooting in one place. Everything here applies to the app you already have - no account needed to read any of it.
guidePage.footerNote: Not covered here? Support replies to real email, not a ticket queue.

sections.title: Getting started
sections.desc: Install it, get your files in, and know where your progress lives.

items.q: How do I add books and folders to BiblioFuse on iPhone?
items.a: BiblioFuse stores files in its own iCloud-synced folder. You can add books via the Files app (copy files into the BiblioFuse folder), via AirDrop, or via the built-in Wi-Fi Transfer — open a library session from Mac or PC and drag files in from any browser.

items.q: Where are reading progress, bookmarks, ratings, and tags saved?
items.a: It depends on where the book file lives:

bullets.text: Local storage — saved on that device only, no cross-device sync
iCloud storage — saved to iCloud, syncs across all iOS, Mac, and PC devices automatically
SMB / network share (Mac or PC streaming) — saved on the host device
sub: iOS reading a Mac stream: progress saves on the Mac
iOS reading a PC stream: progress saves on the PC
PC ↔ Mac: stored independently — they do not share data
If you use both Mac and PC as streaming hosts, your reading data will be split. Stick to one host for consistency.

links.label: Reading CBZ and CBR on iPhone

sections.title: Libraries & servers
sections.desc: Kavita, Komga and any OPDS catalogue, plus folder-as-library browsing.

links.label: Kavita & Komga setup QR generator
links.note: Skip typing a server URL and API key on a phone.

sections.title: Streaming from your Mac or PC
sections.desc: Your own machine hosts the library; the app reads from it.

items.q: How does streaming from Mac or PC to iPhone work?
items.a: Your Mac or PC runs a local server and writes the connection address to iCloud Drive. Your iPhone picks it up automatically. Both devices must have Tailscale on (works at home and remotely). If only one device has Tailscale on, the connection will fail. Keeping both devices always on Tailscale gives the most consistent experience.

items.q: What do I need to set up streaming?
items.a: It depends on where you want to read.

sub: The host app on your Mac or PC advertises itself on your local network; your iPhone, iPad or Vision Pro finds it on its own.
Allow local network access the first time the app asks. That is the whole setup.

bullets.text: Away from home — the same iCloud account on both devices, plus Tailscale running on both.
sub: The host writes its address to your iCloud Drive and the reading device picks it up over Tailscale.
Windows has no built-in iCloud — install iCloud for Windows from the Microsoft Store.
Your iCloud and Tailscale accounts can use different email addresses, and a Tailscale exit node is not needed.

bullets.text: A NAS host works differently — it has no iCloud path at all.
sub: Pair it once on your local network so the certificate is stored, after which the same host can be reached remotely over Tailscale.

items.q: Streaming is set up correctly but the host does not appear — what should I try?
items.a: Stale address files used to be the usual cause. The Mac host now clears them by itself every time streaming starts, stops, or its address changes — including iCloud conflict copies — so this is rarely the problem any more.

bullets.text: Quit and reopen the app on the host. It republishes a fresh address on launch.
On the reading device, open the streaming source list and look for a green dot beside the host name.
sub: Grey means the host has not been reached yet — wait a few seconds, or force-quit and reopen the app on the host.

bullets.text: The Windows host does not yet do that automatic cleanup.
sub: If a PC host stays invisible, open iCloud Drive → BiblioFuse → Documents from an iPhone or Mac and delete stream_endpoint.json along with any numbered copies, then reopen the host app.
Do this from an iPhone or Mac rather than the PC — Windows may hold only an online-only placeholder, so deleting there is unreliable.

items.q: Do I need Tailscale to stream at home?
items.a: No. Local Wi-Fi streaming works on its own — the host advertises itself on your network and the app connects to it over HTTPS with a pinned certificate. Early versions genuinely did fail on a local network, because the app was not reading the metadata the host advertised and fell back to a plain-HTTP address that release builds block. That is fixed. Tailscale is now only for reading away from home.

bullets.text: Settings → Mac / PC Streaming has three modes.
sub: iCloud + Tailscale — lists both local hosts and the remote one published through iCloud.
Local Wi-Fi — local hosts only; no remote address is ever shown or dialled.
Manual Tailscale — for a host you enter by hand, including a NAS.

bullets.text: There is deliberately no automatic switching between local and remote.
sub: On the same network both entries appear for the same host and you pick one, so a working local connection is never silently swapped for a slower route.
tvOS cannot use iCloud Documents, and the Tailscale path is built and tested but shipped switched off while an upstream Tailscale bug on tvOS is unresolved.

items.q: Can Android read from a Mac or PC host?
items.a: Yes. The Android app finds hosts on your local network, or you can type the host address in by hand, and it can copy a book from the host into its own library. Reading position is sent back to the host. Android has no iCloud access, so reading away from home means entering the host address manually over Tailscale rather than having it discovered for you.

sections.title: Reading
sections.desc: Formats, reading direction, text-to-speech and translation.

items.q: Does BiblioFuse work on Apple Vision Pro?
items.a: Yes. BiblioFuse is a native visionOS app on the App Store — a true spatial window, not a compatibility-mode iPad app. It supports eye tracking, pinch, mouse, trackpad, and keyboard, and it is included in the universal iOS + Mac purchase at no extra cost.

items.q: What spatial reading layouts does BiblioFuse support on visionOS?
items.a: Three spatial library layouts: Spatial Bookshelves (your covers on floating shelves), Grid View (a floating grid for large libraries), and Slanted Wall (an angled gallery wall with rating and tag filters). You can also stream your library from a Mac or PC to keep Vision Pro storage free.

items.q: How do I get better text-to-speech voices in BiblioFuse?
items.a: Higher-quality voices may already be available through your device's text-to-speech system, but some must be downloaded separately. BiblioFuse will detect newly installed voices automatically when they are made available to apps.

sub: Go to Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → Voices
Choose your language, then download an Enhanced or Premium voice
Premium voices on supported iOS versions provide Apple's highest-quality speech
Go to Settings → Accessibility → Text-to-speech output
Depending on your device, this setting may instead appear under Settings → General management → Text-to-speech, or Settings → System → Languages → Text-to-speech output
Select your preferred text-to-speech engine, such as Speech Recognition & Synthesis from Google or your device manufacturer's engine
Open the engine settings, select Install voice data, and download the languages or voices you want
You may also update the text-to-speech engine through Google Play
Voice quality and availability vary by device, language, manufacturer, and installed TTS engine — some higher-quality voices may require an internet connection
Restart BiblioFuse, then begin a new TTS session
Go to System Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → System Voice → Manage Voices
Download any Enhanced or Premium voice for your language
Go to Settings → Time & language → Language & region
Add your reading language, or open Language options for an installed language
Under Language features, install Text-to-speech
Restart BiblioFuse, then begin a new TTS session
Go to Settings → Accessibility → Narrator
Under Add natural voices, download the voice you want
Windows may expose some Natural voices only to Narrator and not to other applications

bullets.text: No BiblioFuse update is required. BiblioFuse detects newly installed voices when they are exposed through the Android, Apple, or Windows text-to-speech system

items.q: What is the difference between the PC Reader and the PC EPUB / CBZ tools?
items.a: The PC Reader is a full reading app — it opens books, manages your library, compresses files, and streams to iPhone. The PC EPUB and CBZ tools are lighter, cheaper apps focused on compression and merging only, with no reader.
